Health & fitness / Army Body Fat

Army Body Fat Calculator

Calculate waist-to-height ratio using the Army’s current body-composition screening measure and compare it with the published 0.55 standard. The tool does not estimate body-fat percentage; the Army replaced its former circumference tape test with this ratio in 2026. Waist-to-height ratio = abdominal circumference at the navel ÷ height, using the same unit for both. Current Army guidance sets a screening standard below 0.55.

How to use this calculator

  1. Enter abdominal circumference at navel, height.
  2. Select Calculate to see the answer and its breakdown.
  3. Keep a scenario, change an input and compare the results.

Use consistent units and check the assumptions below before applying the result.

How army body fat is calculated

Waist-to-height ratio = abdominal circumference at the navel ÷ height, using the same unit for both. Current Army guidance sets a screening standard below 0.55. A 36-inch waist and 70-inch height produce a ratio of 0.514, below 0.55.

Waist-to-height ratio=navel waist/height; current Army screen is below 0.55.
A worked example

A 36-inch waist and 70-inch height produce a ratio of 0.514, below 0.55.

Assumptions & useful context

Current Army body-composition screening measure; this is not a body-fat percentage or official assessment.

Health calculations are estimates for education. They cannot diagnose a condition or replace a clinician’s assessment. Individual needs vary, especially during pregnancy, illness and growth.

U.S. Army: Body Composition Program policy update

Frequently asked questions

Does this return a body-fat percentage?

No. It calculates the current Army screening ratio.

Is this an official Army assessment?

No. Official measurements and eligibility decisions follow Army procedures.
